headline: Antetokounmpo has 22 points and 23 rebounds as the Heat stop the Knicks' 6-game winning streak
text: NEW YORK -- — Giannis Antetokounmpo had 22 points and a career-high 23 rebounds, Bam Adebayo scored 25 points and the Miami Heat ended the New York Knicks ' six-game winning streak and NBA Cup title reign with a 108-105 victory Friday night. The Knicks erased a 23-point deficit to grab the lead in the fourth quarter, but Jalen Brunson hit only two of three free throws when he was fouled shooting a 3-pointer with 9.8 seconds remaining and the Heat held on. Miami would have won its group and advanced to the quarterfinals if Philadelphia had lost in Indiana, but the 76ers beat the Pacers 111-87. Brunson had 27 points and eight assists for the Knicks, who needed to win by at least seven points and have the 76ers lose to have a chance to become the first team to advance to the knockout round of the tournament with a 2-2 record. Karl-Anthony Towns had 19 points and 10 rebounds while playing with an abdominal injury that had him listed as questionable until shortly before the game and wincing in pain a few times during it. The Heat went 6 for 11 on 3s and the Knicks were 2 for 11 in the first quarter as Miami led 31-21. Towns got the first two baskets of the second before the Heat ran off 15 straight points for a 46-25 advantage. It was 58-35 after Adebayo's basket with 2:06 remaining, but the Knicks gained a little ground while Antetokounmpo was on the bench with three fouls and cut it to 60-44 at halftime. The Knicks got back in it with a 9-0 run early in the third quarter and went ahead 92-91 midway through the fourth. Adebayo's basket snapped a 95-all tie with 4:02 to play and the Heat stayed ahead from there. Up next Heat: Visit Cleveland on Sunday. Knicks: Host Atlanta on Sunday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Isaiah Joe scores 22 points, Pistons' reserves power NBA Cup win over Bucks
text: DETROIT -- — Isaiah Joe scored 22 points to help the Detroit Pistons overcome a slow start and beat the Milwaukee Bucks 113-98 in an NBA Cup game Friday night. The Pistons won East Group A at 3-1 with a better points differential than the Toronto Raptors and Orlando Magic . Detroit will host a knockout-round game and could finish with the Eastern Conference's top seed. The Bucks finished 0-4 in group play. The Pistons, who finished with seven players in double figures, were missing three starters — Jalen Duren (hamstring) and Duncan Robinson (quadriceps) have been out for weeks, and Cade Cunningham (knee) also was in street clothes. Paul Reed and fellow reserve Elijah Harkless added 14 points. Detroit had 60 bench points while the starters finished with 53. Rookie Brayden Burries had 23 points for the Bucks and Tyler Herro added 20. Milwaukee led by 16 points in the first quarter, but only had a two-point advantage at halftime. The Pistons then put up a 42-point third quarter that included points from eight players. Daniss Jenkins ' 3-pointer at the buzzer put Detroit up 90-78 at quarter's end. Officials and coaches had to jump in between the players midway through the fourth after Myles Turner fired a ball into Ausar Thompson 's back. Both players were given technical fouls. After the confrontation, the game turned into a dunk fest for the Pistons, who got points from nine players in an 64-point second half. The Bucks had a rare good start, taking a 19-3 lead before Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff pulled all of his starters. The reserves got Detroit back into the game, then went on a 15-2 run to take the lead in the second quarter. Milwaukee led 50-48 at halftime, with Detroit's starters only contributing 12 points. Up next Bucks: Host Oklahoma City on Saturday night. Pistons: Host Orlando on Sunday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: LeBron James and 76ers breeze past Pacers 111-87, advance to NBA Cup knockout round
text: INDIANAPOLIS -- — LeBron James had 21 points, seven rebounds and six assists, and the Philadelphia 76ers breezed past the Indiana Pacers 111-87 on Friday night to win East Group B and advance to the knockout round of the NBA Cup . The Sixers will play at East Group C winner Atlanta next week in the quarterfinals of the NBA's in-season tournament. Joel Embiid added 14 points and 11 rebounds for the Eastern Conference-leading Sixers (16-4), who have won seven of eight. James hit three 3-pointers in the opening four minutes and scored 11 points in the first quarter as the Sixers never trailed. He finished 8 of 13 from the floor in 27 minutes. Anfernee Simons added 19 points for Philadelphia, Tyrese Maxey scored 14 and Dominick Barlow had 12. Jay Huff scored 18 points and Andrew Nembhard added 14 for Indiana, which made its fewest 3-pointers of the season, going 5 of 37 (13.5%) from beyond the arc. The Pacers beat Oklahoma City on Monday night but have lost five of six. Ivica Zubac had 16 rebounds for Indiana. Philadelphia shot 15 of 37 (40.5%) from 3-point range. Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton is practicing with the team as he rehabs from a left hamstring strain but missed his 15th straight game. He last played on Oct. 26. Up next 76ers: At Houston on Saturday night. Pacers: At Chicago on Saturday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Raptors beat Nets in final NBA Cup group-stage game for both teams
text: TORONTO -- — Scottie Barnes scored 34 points and the Toronto Raptors beat the Brooklyn Nets 124-100 on Friday night in the final NBA Cup group-stage game for both teams. The Raptors finished the game holding the Eastern Conference wild-card berth at 3-1, but dropped out when Atlanta beat Boston a few minutes later. The Celtics had a higher point differential than the Raptors. Immanuel Quickley had a triple-double with 24 points, a season-high 14 assists and 10 rebounds for Toronto (7-11). Collin Murray-Boyles came off the bench for 19 points and seven rebounds. Ja’Kobe Walter left the game in the third quarter because of a right quad contusion. He finished with three points, three rebounds and three assists in 24 minutes. Julius Randle and Mikel Brown Jr . scored 21 points apiece for Brooklyn (4-14). Michael Porter Jr . added 17 points. Up next Nets: At Charlotte on Saturday night. Raptors: Host Denver on Sunday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Johnson helps Hawks close out NBA Cup group stage with 87-86 win over Celtics
text: BOSTON -- — Jalen Johnson had 24 points, Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored Atlanta’s final four points as part of a 20-point night and the Hawks beat the Boston Celtics 87-86 on Friday in the final NBA Cup group-stage game for both teams. The Celtics and Hawks finished 3-1 in Cup play, with Atlanta winning the group thanks to taking the head-to-head matchup against Boston. The Hawks have won five straight. Alexander-Walker finished off a drive with 54.3 seconds left to break a tie, then sealed it with two free throws that made it a four-point game with 2.6 seconds remaining. Atlanta held Boston to 35 points in the second half. For the game, the Celtics shot 41% and committed 26 turnovers, with Jayson Tatum losing the ball with 3.8 seconds left and Boston down two. Tatum had 20 points, but went scoreless in the fourth quarter. Celtics guard Derrick White tossed in a three-pointer at the buzzer as part of a 13-point night. With Boston’s Mitchell Robinson out for the fourth straight game due to a COVID-19 illness, Neemias Queta once again started center and a career-high 22 rebounds along with 11 points. The Hawks (12-6) came in hot but couldn’t shake a cold spell in the first half. They opened the game missing 11 of 12 shots and 15 of 20 and entered halftime trailing 51-39 after shooting 28% from the field and missing 19 of 25 from 3. Trailing 65-50, Atlanta went on a 20-4 run that closed the third quarter and saw the Celtics (12-7) trail for the first time in the game. The Celtics have dropped five of six. Up next Hawks: At New York on Sunday. Celtics: At San Antonio on Sunday. ------

headline: Grizzlies top Timberwolves 114-109 to win NBA Cup West Group B
text: MINNEAPOLIS -- — Cedric Coward scored 22 points, Javon Small tied a season high with 19 points off the bench, and the Memphis Grizzlies won the NBA Cup West Group B on Friday with a 114-109 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves . Ty Jerome added 18 points and Cam Spencer 16 for the Grizzlies, winners in eight of their past nine games. Ayo Dosunmu led Minnesota with 27 points and eight assists. Jonathan Kuminga scored 19 points and Bones Hyland had 16 off the bench for the Timberwolves, whoh made just 14 of 23 free throws. Minnesota entered the game shooting a league-worst 69.6% from the line. Already without the injured Anthony Edwards , Minnesota played without top guard LaMelo Ball , who sprained his left ankle in Wednesday’s win at Oklahoma City and is considered day to day. Ball is averaging 17.3 points per game and a team-high 5.7 assists. Coward and Spencer scored seven points in a 21-6 Memphis surge to start the fourth quarter for a 99-87 lead with less than seven minutes to play. A pair of steals and layups by Dosunmu cut the deficit to 109-105 with 31 seconds left, but the Timberwolves got no closer. Memphis center Zach Edey , who left Wednesday’s game in the first half due to left ankle soreness, started and scored five points in 12 minutes before fouling out. Down by 14 late in the first half, Minnesota started the third quarter on a 26-11 run for a 76-72 lead, capped by Kuminga's transition dunk after a block by Joan Beringer of a Small drive. Jaden McDaniels scored 13 points for Minnesota before fouling out. He scored 91 points combined in his previous three games. Up Next Grizzlies: Home against the Los Angeles Lakers on Sunday. Timberwolves: At Sacramento on Sunday to start a three-game road trip. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Cooper Flagg leads Mavericks' rally to beat Suns, finish 4-0 in NBA Cup group play
text: PHOENIX -- — Cooper Flagg scored 34 points and led a late Dallas charge in a 113-109 victory over the Phoenix Suns that left the Mavericks perfect in NBA Cup group play. Dallas had already wrapped up West Group A by winning its first three Cup games. The Suns were 1/3 in the competition, squandering a 21-point lead against the Mavericks. Flagg also has eight assists, seven rebounds, five steals and four blocks in just under 42 minutes. Dallas has won five in a row. Devin Booker led Phoenix with 31 points. Flagg hit a 16-footer to pull Dallas to 106-105 with 1:24 left. After Booker missed a 3-point attempt, Flagg put the Mavericks ahead with a tip-in with 56 seconds left. After Booker missed a 16-footer, Flagg made a turnaround jumper with 22.6 left for a 109-106 lead, and Max Christie made two free throws to push the lead to five. Booker made a 3-pointer to cut it to 111-109 with five seconds remaining. Christie made two more free throws to put it away. Christie finished with 16 points, and Naji Marshall had 14. Collin Gillespie added 14 points for Phoenix, back home after winning four of five on a trip. Up next Mavericks: Host Boston on Monday night. Suns: At Utah on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Spurs ride second-half surge to earn spot in NBA Cup knockout round with 99-96 victory over Lakers
text: SAN ANTONIO -- — Stephon Castle had 26 points, Victor Wembanyama had 25 points and 16 rebounds, and the San Antonio Spurs surged in the second half for a 99-96 win over the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday night to advance to the NBA Cup knockout round. Castle was 10 for 15 from the field, including a 3-pointer that put San Antonio up 96-90 with 43.4 seconds remaining following De’Aaron Fox’s rebound of Wembanyama’s missed free throw. Luka Doncic had 31 points to lead Los Angeles, which was eliminated from the NBA Cup with the loss. Austin Reaves added 21 points and Walker Kessler had 10 points and 13 rebounds. Reaves was 5 for 9 on 3-pointers, including a 25-footer with 34 seconds remaining that cut the Spurs’ lead to 96-93. Jake LaRavia hit a pair of free throws after Fox lost possession on a double dribble. Fox responded with a pair of free throws with 6.6 seconds left that put the Spurs up 98-95. San Antonio overcame an anemic first half, outscoring Los Angeles 30-14 in the third quarter with Keldon Johnson’s 3-pointer with two seconds remaining tying the game at 68 entering the fourth. The Lakers took a 27-14 lead in the opening period as the Spurs shot 7 for 18 in posting a season-low for points in any quarter this season. San Antonio also set a season-low for any half in trailing 54-38 at halftime. Castle hit consecutive 3-pointers to put San Antonio ahead 81-73 with his second 3 coming after Carter Bryant went soaring through the lane for an offensive rebound. Bryant finished with three points, three rebounds and several key defensive plays during the Spurs' rally. San Antonio lost to the New York Knicks in last season’s NBA Cup final. Up next Lakers: At Memphis on Sunday. Spurs: Host Boston on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Jamal Murray scores 36 to lead Nuggets past Jazz 120-107
text: SALT LAKE CITY -- — Jamal Murray scored 36 points to rally the Denver Nuggets to a 120-107 victory over the Utah Jazz in NBA Cup group play on Friday night. Nikola Jokic tallied 17 points, 15 assists, and nine rebounds for the Nuggets. Christian Braun added 20 points and eight rebounds. Keyonte George scored 25 points and Darryn Peterson added 20 to lead the Jazz. Svi Mykhailiuk added 18 points off the bench. Jusuf Nurkic made his season debut after missing Utah’s first 19 games with a toe injury and finished with a team-high 11 assists. Nurkic’s crisp passing helped elevate the Jazz offense following a sluggish start. Utah seized a 102-97 lead after Ace Bailey threw down an alley oop dunk to punctuate a string of three straight baskets for the Jazz. Denver erased the deficit behind an 11-0 run, taking a 108-104 lead with 3:25 left on Murray’s step-back 3-pointer that capped the run. Mykhailiuk cut it back to one on a 3, but Utah drew no closer after the Nuggets scored on five straight possessions, punctuated by Murray’s finger roll layup and free throw. Denver staked out a 24-10 lead deep into the first quarter behind a hot start from Jokic. He scored three baskets and assisted on three others to help the Nuggets take control early. Utah chipped away at the deficit and finally took their first lead at 31-29 early in the second quarter when Brice Sensabaugh capped a 9-2 run with a 3-pointer. The Jazz traded baskets with the Nuggets and led through most of the third quarter, going up by as many as six points when Mykhailiuk drove for a layup to put Utah up 81-75. Up Next Nuggets: At Toronto on Sunday. Jazz: Host Phoenix on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Pelicans beat Clippers 105-104 in NBA Cup group finale
text: INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III each scored 25 points and the New Orleans Pelicans beat the Los Angeles Clippers 105-104 on Friday night in their NBA Cup group finale. Both teams were 1/3 in group play. Williamson was 11 of 15 from the field and had seven rebounds and five assists. Murphy was 9 of 16 and had six steals. Darius Garland led Los Angeles with 19 points. Brook Lopez had 17, hitting a 3-pointer in the final second to make it a one-point game. The Pelicans snapped a four-game losing streak to improve to 6-14. The Clippers have lost six in a row to fall to 4-14. Up next Pelicans: At Portland on Sunday. Clippers: At Golden State on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Trail Blazers beat the Warriors 116-94 to advance to the NBA Cup quarterfinals
text: PORTLAND, Ore. -- — Deni Avdija had 26 points and eight rebounds, Toumani Camara added 20 points and eight rebounds and the Portland Trail Blazers beat the Golden State Warriors 116-94 on Friday night to advance to the NBA Cup quarterfinals. Portland led by 36 points in the first half and Golden State cut it to 10 in the fourth quarter before Portland regained control. With its margin of victory and San Antonio’s win over the Lakers, Portland will host the Memphis Grizzlies on Dec. 5. Scoot Henderson added 18 points for Portland off the bench. Yaxel Lendeborg led the Warriors with 18 points. Golden State is playing without Stephen Curry as he recovers from a torn oblique muscle. Portland jumped out to a 37-11 first quarter lead as the Warriors shot 4 for 24 from the field and committed six turnovers in the first quarter. Portland started the second quarter with a 10-0 run and pushed their lead to 36 at 47-11. The Warriors mounted their comeback in stages, starting with a 13-2 run to cut the lead to 49-24. Lendeborg cut the lead to 12 on a 3-pointer with 2:39 left in the third quarter at 88-76. The Warriors cut the lead to 10 one more time on a layup by Lendeborg with just over five minutes left. Portland’s Damian Lillard did not play with right calf tightness, which coach Micah Nori said was a “day-to-day,” situation. Up next Warriors; Hosts the Los Angeles Clippers on Friday night. Trail Blazers: Host New Orleans on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
